subject: Order form redlines — output ownership / training exclusions
messages:
From: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@orionhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: tim.blake@orionhealth.com, legal@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — IP & training questions

Jonas — thanks for sending the draft. A couple of urgent asks from our side as we finalize procurement: 

1) Output ownership: Our legal team (cc'd) is asking for explicit assignment of output ownership for content generated by our product flows. Can Redwood confirm whether you will assign title to Orion for outputs created by Orion users? If not, can you accept a perpetual, transferable right to use and exploit outputs?

2) Training / model use: We need a firm commitment that Orion's customer content will not be used to further train Redwood-hosted models unless we opt-in via an explicit agreement. The current Order Form language is ambiguous.

3) Feedback / telemetry: We are okay with aggregated telemetry but need assurances that telemetry cannot be tied back to patient data (PHI). If you require telemetry for product improvements, we need an evidence table describing fields collected and retention windows.

I've attached our redlines to the Order Form (Orion_OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf) — please review and let us know what Redwood can accept. Prefer a short call if it helps.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Wong
Head of Product Operations
Orion Health Systems

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. Quick notes before legal takes a pass: 

- Output: Our standard position is to grant customers broad rights to use outputs (including commercial use) but not an assignment of model IP. We can offer a perpetual, nonexclusive, transferable license to outputs produced by Orion's calls. If Orion needs assignment instead of license, that is a commercial exception and will require procurement/finance approval.

- Training: We can confirm a default "no training" stance for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted API, we can add an opt-out mechanism and a contractual commitment not to use customer content to train models unless Orion provides opt-in consent. We will need to map this to operational controls (tagging, retention).

- Telemetry/Evidence: Attaching our suggested response (Redwood_Response_OrderForm_v2.docx) and a proposed telemetry matrix. Laura — can you please review the redline and the proposed language in section 4 (Output Rights) and section 7 (Model Use / Data)? Also flag any commercial exceptions required for assignment requests.

If it helps, happy to set a 30-min sync with Orion legal tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Team — I've reviewed Orion's redlines and Jonas's response. Summary of legal positions and recommended edits below. Key open points are bolded.

1) Output ownership (Order Form §4):
- Proposed Redwood language: "Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, modify and commercialize Outputs generated by Customer Data." This preserves our model code/IP while giving the customer rights they need.
- Orion asked for assignment. Our stance: no assignment of model or service IP. Assignment of Outputs only (if they define "Outputs" narrowly) could be acceptable as a negotiated exception. Any assignment request must be escalated to Sales leadership and Finance for revenue impact.

2) Training & Model Use (Order Form §7):
- For hosted API customers: add explicit "no training without consent" clause and a mechanism for operational opt-out. We will accept the requested language with the following additions:
  * Redwood will implement a tagged bucket to ensure data marked as "NoTrain" is excluded from training pipelines.
  * Retention: customer content will be deleted from ephemeral caches within 7 days unless otherwise required for billing/ops. (We need Ops to confirm feasibility.)

3) Feedback license / improvements (Order Form §8):
- Limit license to aggregated, de-identified feedback. Include an explicit PHI carveout: "Redwood shall not use PHI as Feedback or to train models; any telemetry that could reasonably be re-identified will be excluded."

4) Evidence & Telemetry (attachment):
- Good ask. I've annotated the telemetry matrix and marked fields that present PHI risk. Monica / Priyom — please confirm the operational steps and retention windows that we can commit to in contract.

Action items: 
- Ben: commercial impact for assignment exception? (If customer insists, what price uplift?)
- Monica & Priyom: Ops confirmation on tag-based opt-out and 7-day cache deletion, plus any infra constraints to be surfaced by EOD Monday.
- Jonas: propose a time window for a 30-min legal sync with Orion.

If Orion signs off on license (not assignment) + our technical opt-out, we can proceed to final Order Form. If Orion insists on assignment, I'll need written rationale and approval from Sales leadership for exceptions.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts (Redwood Inference)
